papers.title: Neural Learning of Fast Matrix Multiplication Algorithms: a Geometric Perspective
papers.abstract: We combine neural learning and geometric diagnostics to investigate the rank and border rank of the \(3\times3\) matrix-multiplication tensor \(M_3\). Using the Bhattacharya--Mesner product, we derive \textsc{MatMulNet}, a differentiable architecture encoding bilinear maps. Constrained refinement yields a length-\(23\) numerical solution with machine-precision full-tensor residual and bounded decomposition weight. Along the explored length-\(22\) branch, the residual instead decreases as the gauge-invariant weight grows. This contrast supports \(R_{\mathbb R}(M_3)=23\) as a working hypothesis. A Laurent-parametrised extension probes border rank, giving a tentative, protocol-dependent motivation to investigate \(r=19\) and the adjacent \(r=18\) case. For \(M_4\), the same diagnostics distinguish bounded numerical solutions recovered from perturbed known schemes, structured residual plateaus, and weight-growing approximations, revealing the dependence of the search on initialisation. Together, the experiments connect approximation accuracy with decomposition growth and identify concrete targets for exact or certified investigation.

papers.title: On Higher-Order Geometric Refinements of Classical Covariance Asymptotics: An Approach via Intrinsic and Extrinsic Information Geometry
papers.abstract: Classical Fisher-information asymptotics describe the covariance of regular efficient estimators through the local quadratic approximation of the log-likelihood, and thus capture first-order geometry only. In curved models, including mixtures, curved exponential families, latent-variable models, and manifold-constrained parameter spaces, finite-sample behavior can deviate systematically from these predictions. We develop a coordinate-invariant, curvature-aware refinement by viewing a regular parametric family as a Riemannian manifold \((\Theta,g)\) with Fisher--Rao metric, immersed in \(L^2(\mu)\) through the square-root density map. Under suitable regularity and moment assumptions, we derive an \(n^{-2}\) correction to the leading \(n^{-1}I(\theta)^{-1}\) covariance term for score-root, first-order efficient estimators. The correction is governed by a tensor \(P_{ij}\) that decomposes canonically into three parts, an intrinsic Ricci-type contraction of the Fisher--Rao curvature tensor, an extrinsic Gram-type contraction of the second fundamental form, and a Hellinger discrepancy tensor encoding higher-order probabilistic information not determined by immersion geometry alone. The extrinsic term is positive semidefinite, the full correction is invariant under smooth reparameterization, and it vanishes identically for full exponential families. We then extend the picture to singular models, where Fisher information degenerates. Using resolution of singularities under an additive normal crossing assumption, we describe the resolved metric, the role of the real log canonical threshold in learning rates and posterior mean-squared error, and a curvature-based covariance expansion on the resolved space that recovers the regular theory as a special case. This framework also suggests geometric diagnostics of weak identifiability and curvature-aware principles for regularization and optimization.

papers.title: Raynaud and Gruson's flattening techniques in Berkovich geometry
papers.abstract: Raynaud and Gruson introduced a flattening procedure for coherent sheaf in the schemes context that rely on sophisticated techniques of algebra and geometry. These methods were later used by Raynaud, Bosch and L\"utkebohmert in formal geometry, and more recently Ducros has developed analogous tools for Berkovich spaces. However, it should be noted that the expression "flattening by blowing up" is, in this context, a little abusive because the flattening process actually requires a succession of blow up and quasi-\'etale morphisms. The aim of this article is to develop a local flattening technique in Berkovich geometry, in the boundaryless case, which only involves blow up.

papers.title: Spaces of ratios of schemes and \'etale cohomology
papers.abstract: We introduce the arithmetic topologies on the spaces of ratios for log schemes and prove the basic properties of their cohomologies.

papers.title: On the tensor product of semistable Hermitian adelic vector bundles over an adelic curve
papers.abstract: We prove tensor semistability for Hermitian adelic vector bundles on proper adelic curves whose underlying fields are countable and of characteristic zero. The central estimate concerns the canonical integral Specht lattice of a rectangular partition with fixed height: its logarithmic covolume, divided by its rank and tensor degree, tends to zero. We prove this estimate from monic seminormal norms and an exact hypergeometric law weighted by the square of a Vandermonde product for tableau prefixes. Constant adelic Specht bundles and equivariant contractions then yield the slope inequality for every geometrically semistable subspace of a finite tensor product. The correction is the measure of the Archimedean places times a sublinear Specht term and vanishes in the limit as the auxiliary degree tends to infinity. An instability-filtration argument completes the reduction to arbitrary factors and identifies the tensor product Harder--Narasimhan filtration. The number field specialization gives the Bost tensor semistability conjecture in all ranks.

papers.title: Stably irrational algebraically elliptic Fano threefolds
papers.abstract: We establish algebraic ellipticity in the sense of Gromov of a general hypersurface of bidegree $(2,2)$ in $\mathbb P^2\times\mathbb P^2$. According to a theorem of B\"ohning and Graf von Bothmer, a very general such hypersurface is a stably irrational Fano threefold.

papers.title: Arithmetic jet stacks
papers.abstract: We construct a stack, which generalizes the notion of the arithmetic jet space functor constructed by Borger using the generalized Witt vector constructions. A priori we con- struct the jet space functor for prestacks, consequently showing that this functor preserves stacks. We then proceed to show the representability of the jet space functor applied to a representable morphism of stacks thereby showing that the jet space functor preserves algebraic and Deligne-Mumford Stacks. We also discuss the properties of morphisms preserved under the jet functor

papers.title: Tannakian Brill-Noether theory of nodal curves
papers.abstract: Using the Tannakian categories arising from convolutions of perverse sheaves on semi-abelian varieties, we can associate to any subvariety of a semi-abelian variety a reductive group together with a representation. We compute these groups and representations for Brill-Noether varieties of all curves whose generalized Jacobian is semi-abelian, in particular for nodal curves. We also obtain new results on the dimension and non-degeneracy of these Brill-Noether varieties.

papers.title: Torrelli's Question for Isolated Hypersurface Singularities
papers.abstract: Torrelli asked whether the class $[1/f]$ belongs to the intersection homology $\mathcal{D}$-module of a hypersurface if and only if $-1$ is a simple root of its local Bernstein-Sato polynomial. We prove this equivalence for isolated hypersurface germs with $2\le n\le 4$ variables, and we construct isolated counterexamples with $n$ variables for every $n\ge 5$. In fact a counterexample with $[1/f]\in\mathrm{IC}_D$ and $\mathrm{mult}_{s=-1}b_f(s)=r\ge 2$ always needs at least $r+3$ variables. The counterexamples modify a three-variable example of Saito and adjoin suitable pure powers in the new variables. We also show that a counterexample polynomial in $n$ variables needs at least $n+1$ monomials, and we record further cases in which the equivalence holds.

papers.title: Finite abelian groups acting on rationally connected threefolds III: Classification
papers.abstract: We complete the classification of finite abelian groups that admit a faithful action on a rationally connected threefold. For a finite abelian group $G$ with invariant factors $1<d_1\mid\cdots\mid d_s$, put $c(G)=\sum_i(1-1/d_i)$. We prove that for $1\le n\le3$ such a group admits a faithful action on a rationally connected variety of dimension $n$ if and only if $c(G)\le n$. We also show that finite abelian subgroups of the Cremona group of rank three are, up to isomorphism, precisely the products of finite abelian subgroups of the Cremona groups of ranks one and two. Four further groups can act faithfully on rationally connected threefolds. For each of these groups, the faithful action is unique up to birational conjugacy and automorphism of the acting group.

papers.title: Automorphism groups of Severi--Brauer varieties of odd prime degree over $\mathbb{Q}$
papers.abstract: We prove that the only non-trivial finite subgroup of automorphism group of non-trivial Severi--Brauer variety of odd prime degree $p$ over the field of rational numbers is $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}.$

papers.title: Note on OpenAI's proof of the base of Lagrangian fibrations
papers.abstract: OpenAI proved that every Lagrangian fibration of a compact hyper-K\"ahler manifold has a base $\mathbb P^n$. This expository note summarizes the last section of their paper.

papers.title: Strong holonomicity of functions on curves
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth affine irreducible curve over $\mathbb C$, and let ${\mathcal D} = {\mathcal D} (X)$ be the ring of global differential operators on $X$. To every nonzero operator $L \in {\mathcal D} $ we attach a non-negative integer $n(L)$, the holonomicity index of $L$, which is defined in an elementary way, by counting solutions of $L$ in the truncated local rings at the singular points of $L$. Our main theorem shows that $n(L)$ coincides with the Calogero--Moser index of the Weyl closure ${\rm cl}(L) = {\mathcal D}(K) \cap {\mathcal D} $ of $L$, i.e. with the integer $n$ labelling the Calogero--Moser space $ {\mathcal C}_n(X,\mathcal{I})$ that contains the isomorphism class of the left ideal ${\rm cl}(L)$ under the classification of ideals of ${\mathcal D}$ given in [Berest--Chalykh, 2012]. The proof is based on a dual version of the Cannings--Holland correspondence, which describes left ideals of ${\mathcal D}$ in terms of finite-dimensional spaces of algebraic distributions on $X$, and an explicit formula for the Calogero--Moser index given in terms of these distributions. We apply these results to annihilators of locally holomorphic functions on $X$: we call a holonomic function $f$ strongly holonomic if the Calogero--Moser index of ${\rm Ann}_{\mathcal D}(f)$ is positive, and we compute this index in a number of interesting cases.

papers.title: The local lifting conjecture for dihedral groups of order $2p^n$
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of odd characteristic $p$, and let $D_{p^n}$ denote the dihedral group of order $2p^n$. A local $D_{p^n}$-action is a faithful action of $D_{p^n}$ on the formal power series ring $k[[z]]$ by continuous $k$-automorphisms. The strong Oort conjecture of Chinburg, Guralnick and Harbater predicts that every such action lifts to characteristic zero. This is also the dihedral case of the local lifting conjecture of Obus. We prove this assertion for $n=2$ and every odd prime $p$. More precisely, given a local $D_{p^2}$-action on $k[[z]]$, we construct an action on $R[[Z]]$ by $R$-automorphisms whose reduction modulo the maximal ideal of $R$ is the given action, where $R$ is a complete discrete valuation ring finite over the Witt ring $W(k)$. For arbitrary $n$, let $C_{p^n}$ be the cyclic subgroup of index two in $D_{p^n}$, and let $u_1,\ldots,u_n$ be the upper ramification jumps of $k((z))/k((z))^{C_{p^n}}$. We prove that the action lifts if $u_i\equiv-1\pmod{2p}$ for every $i$. When $p=3$, we also prove lifting under the hypotheses $u_i\equiv5\pmod6$ for $2\leq i<n$ and $3\nmid u_n$.

papers.title: A Determinant Proof of the Sun--Yang--Zuo Conjecture
papers.abstract: We give an elementary proof of the determinant identity in \cite[Conjecture~A.1]{SYZ} over any field of odd characteristic $p$. The proof computes the determinant of a single linear map by dividing by two different monic polynomials. By \cite[Proposition~A.9]{SYZ}, the identity gives another proof of the Sun--Yang--Zuo conjecture. The conjecture identifies the Higgs--de Rham self-map of the four-pointed projective line with the map induced by multiplication by $p$ on its elliptic double cover.

papers.title: Combinatorics of equivariant blowups of spherical varieties
papers.abstract: We explicitly describe the colored fan of the blowup of a smooth spherical variety $X$ along a smooth irreducible $G$-stable subvariety $Y$. The answer is expressed in terms of the colored cone of $Y$ and the localization of the valuation cone at $Y$, and generalizes the star subdivision of fans of toric varieties. We also consider several examples illustrating the main result.

papers.title: The generalized Franchetta conjecture for some hyper-K\"ahler varieties, III
papers.abstract: The generalized Franchetta conjecture states that for a locally complete family of polarized hyper-K\"ahler varieties, the generically defined cycles on any fiber of the universal family over the moduli stack inject into cohomology via the cycle class map. We prove the generalized Franchetta conjecture for the family of double EPW sextics discovered by O'Grady and for the family of double EPW cubes discovered by Iliev-Kapustka-Kapustka-Ranestad. We also prove a Franchetta-type result for the relative square of the universal family of double EPW sextics, which allows to relate double EPW sextics and Gushel-Mukai fourfolds on the level of motives. The proof involves the geometry of Gushel-Mukai fourfolds, whose Kuznetsov component allows to realize double EPW sextics and cubes as moduli spaces of Bridgeland-stable objects, relatively over the parameter space of Gushel-Mukai fourfolds. A key step is that the canonical Chow-K\"unneth decomposition of special Gushel-Mukai fourfolds is multiplicative; we use this to show that generically defined cycles on the third power of a special Gushel-Mukai fourfold inject into cohomology via the cycle class map. Along the way, we also show that the canonical Chow-K\"unneth decomposition of any Gushel-Mukai sixfold is multiplicative.

papers.title: Termination of the Kahler MMP with scaling
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove termination of klt flips with scaling for strongly \(\mathbb Q\)-factorial compact Kahler klt pairs $(X,B)$ with effective \(\mathbb Q\)-boundary. In particular, compact Kahler klt pairs with effective \(\mathbb Q\)-boundary have minimal models when \(K_X+B\) is pseudo-effective, and admit Mori fibre space models otherwise.

papers.title: Around the base ideal and the base locus of a Keller map
papers.abstract: Let $\varphi_F:\Bbbk^n\to\Bbbk^n$ be a Keller map defined by $n$ polynomials $F_1,\ldots,F_n$ in $n$ indeterminates $X=X_1,\ldots,X_n$ over a field $\Bbbk$ of characteristic zero. Miranda-Neto defined the base ideal of $\varphi_F$ as the ideal $I_F$ generated by $F_1,\ldots,F_n$ and the base locus of $\varphi_F$ as the affine algebraic set $V_F=V(I_F)$ determined by the ideal $I_F$. He proved that $I_F$ is a radical ideal, which is a finite intersection of $v_F$ maximal ideals, where ${\rm card}(V_F)\leq v_F$, understanding that $v_F=0$, when $I_F$ is improper. In this paper, we first prove that $v_F\leq \dim_{\Bbbk}(\Bbbk[X]/I_F)\leq [\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$. Using invertible affine transformations on the recent counterexample to the Jacobian Conjecture announced by Alp\"oge, we show that $I_F$ might indeed be improper and that the following cases, $0<{\rm card}(V_F)=v_F<[\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$, $0<{\rm card}(V_F)=v_F=[\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$, $0<{\rm card}(V_F)<v_F<[\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$ and $0={\rm card}(V_F)<v_F<[\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$ might occur. We finish by giving a purely topological equivalent reformulation of the Jacobian Conjecture in terms of the irreducibility of $V_F$.

papers.title: Hodge cycles of Klein hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We study the space of Hodge cycles on Klein varieties. Relating it to the Hodge characters in a covering Fermat variety, we decompose the space of Hodge characters into a part generated by classes of rational subvarieties, and a non-trivial part which we call exceptional. Using Dirichlet characters we show that the exceptional part is always finite. Furthermore, we give sufficient conditions under which there are no exceptional characters, providing infinitely many new cases of the Hodge conjecture for Klein varieties. Finally, we describe the set of exceptional characters of Klein varieties for small dimensions.

papers.title: Grothendieck--Serre for quasi-split groups over two-dimensional regular local rings
papers.abstract: We prove the Grothendieck--Serre conjecture for quasi-split reductive group schemes over two-dimensional regular local rings, that is, every generically trivial torsor under a quasi-split group scheme $G$ over a regular local ring $R$ of dimension two is trivial. Our main result is new when $R$ is ramified and generalizes Nisnevich's result by removing the assumption that the residue field is infinite. By formal patching of torsors and valuative criteria, we are reduced to showing a product formula when $G$ is semisimple and simply connected. Then, we take advantage of relative simple reflections and relative Bruhat decomposition to prove a generation by rank-one subgroups. The analysis on Dynkin diagrams with Galois actions reduces us to $\operatorname{SL}_2$ and three-dimensional $\operatorname{SU}$ factors. For the special unitary case, we treat Hermitian forms by using stabilizations and cancellation to finish the proof.

papers.title: GIT-thresholds for K-moduli spaces of Hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: In this note, we confirm the first wall $c_1(d)$ of K-moduli of hypersurfaces of degree $d$ in $\mathbb P^n$ for $n\geq 3$ and $d\geq n+1$, where $c_1(d)=\frac{n+1}{nd}$ if $d$ is even; and $c_1(d)=\frac{n+1}{nd-(n+1)}$ if $d$ is odd. Before this wall, the K-moduli is identical to the GIT-moduli for degree $d$ hypersurfaces, so we also call this number the GIT-threshold.

papers.title: Free rational curves on singular Fano varieties
papers.abstract: We prove that every klt Fano variety admits a free rational curve in its smooth locus.

papers.title: Rank-Two Attractors and Modularity for a Mirror Bicubic
papers.abstract: We study the mirror family $\mathcal X_\lambda$ of the bicubic Calabi-Yau threefold, obtained from a family of complete intersections of two cubics in $\mathbb P^5$. We show that the four-dimensional weight-three Hodge structure of the fibers over $\lambda^6 = -8$ splits into two rational rank-two pieces of Hodge types $(1,0,0,1)$ and $(0,1,1,0)$; in particular, these points are rank-two attractor points. Using a Hesse pencil fiber-product realization, equivariant point counting, and the Serre-Faltings-Livne method, we identify their semisimplified $\ell$-adic Galois representations with those attached to the weight-four newform $f_{\mathsf{54.4.a.c}}$ and the Tate twist of the weight-two newform $f_{\mathsf{54.2.a.a}}$, where these labels refer to the L-functions and modular forms database.

papers.title: The Tate conjecture for abelian fourfolds
papers.abstract: We prove the Tate conjecture for non-CM and non-ordinary abelian fourfolds over positive characteristic function fields. Combining our previous works (2512.00687 and 2608.28651), this establishes the Tate conjecture for abelian fourfolds over finitely generated fields. Along the way, we classify the $l$-adic monodromy of abelian fourfolds in characteristic $p$ via mixed characteristic lifts and methods from convergent and overconvergent crystalline monodromy, and show that Zarhin's minuscule weights conjecture holds for abelian varieties up to dimension 4. These enable us to prove a characteristic $p$ variant of the Mumford--Tate conjecture for most abelian fourfolds, and reduce the Tate conjecture to Markman's results on the Hodge conjecture.

papers.title: On deformations of foliated complex analytic structures IV-2: Obstructed and unobstructed foliated deformations
papers.abstract: We study foliated deformations of compact complex manifolds with dimension 1-foliations and codimension 1-foliations, and unfoldings of compact complex manifolds with codimension 1-foliations in terms of deformations of sections with classical examples in deformation theory of complex structures.

papers.title: Tropical limits of holomorphic linking for toric hypersurfaces and points
papers.abstract: A holomorphic top form on a smooth hypersurface in a smooth projective toric variety has a unique meromorphic residue lift when the ambient dimension is at least two. Evaluating this lift at a point, relative to the logarithmic volume form, gives a complex linking number. For a one-parameter family of hypersurfaces and a normalised monomial residue, we prove that this function converges to the indicator of the corresponding tropical chamber. The convergence is uniform over compact sets disjoint from the tropical hypersurface, independently of the arguments of the point coordinates. When the chamber is nonempty and its index is an interior lattice point, the limit is the classical linking number of the oriented chamber boundary with the limiting logarithmic point. A plane cubic illustrates both this interpretation and its failure on a tropical wall.

papers.title: Quasi-abelian Cousin groups of number fields:a Galois-orbit criterion and the complete list
papers.abstract: Let K be a number field with at least one complex place. A choice S of one embedding K $\rightarrow$ C at each place embeds the ring of integers of K as a discrete subgroup of Cn, where n is the number of places of K. The quotient T\_K,S is a Cousin group, or a complex torus if K is totally imaginary. We determine exactly when T\_K,S is quasi-abelian. The answer is a Galois criterion: no complex conjugation of the Galois closure of K may interchange two of the chosen complex embeddings. Equivalently, S is lifted from a subfield with at most one complex place above each place of the largest totally real subfield of K. For totally imaginary K this is the theorem of Shimura and Taniyama on abelian varieties with complex multiplication; our results extend it to all number fields. We also obtain the rank of the N{\'e}ron--Severi group, and show that T\_K,S is either quasi-abelian or has only constant meromorphic functions.

papers.title: Functionals commuting with reparametrizations
papers.abstract: Motivated by the study of tangent curve bundles of algebraic varieties, we consider the following simple-looking problem: given a space $E$ of functions, describe functionals from $E^n$ to $E$ which commutes with reparametrizations, i.e. with the right-composition with an element of $E$. Our main result is a complete description of the algebraic solutions of this problem when $E$ is the space of polynomials vanishing in $0$, which we denote by $\mathbb C[T]_0$. This description involves a simple operation, which we call semi-product, with interesting algebraic and geometric properties. The proof involves the study of polyharmonic functions on the positive discrete orthant $\mathbb Z^n_{>0}$, and a relation with the co-invariant algebra of type $A$. We also provide a generalization connected to colored permutations, and discuss the analogue problems where $E=\mathbb C[T]_0/(T^\ell)$ for some $\ell >0$, and where $E$ consists of infinitely differentiable functions. Finding a complete description of algebraic solutions in these settings is still open.

papers.title: Virasoro operators for relative Gromov--Witten theory
papers.abstract: Let $D$ be a smooth divisor in a smooth projective variety $X$. We construct relative Virasoro operators acting on the relative descendant potential of $(X,D)$. Each operator is the logarithmic Virasoro operator of $(X,D)$ plus a boundary correction determined only by $D$ and its normal bundle in $X$. Assuming the Virasoro conjecture for $D$, we prove that the relative constraints are equivalent to the absolute constraints for $X$. Under the same assumption, we establish compatibility with the degeneration formula for two-component projective semistable degenerations satisfying a completeness condition. Consequently, the Virasoro conjecture for the two components and the gluing divisor implies the conjecture for the general fiber. As an application, we prove the Virasoro conjecture for Enriques surfaces in every integral curve class.
